q2pro.note: Part of the Q2PRO crosshair family (ch_scale, ch_alpha, ch_red/green/blue). None of it exists on R1Q2 or vanilla.
Q2PRO also accepts 2, which drives the refresh from the video sync instead of from r_maxfps.

r1q2.note: While cl_async is 0, R1Q2 mirrors cl_maxfps and r_maxfps onto each other, so whichever of the two a config sets last wins for both.

cl_async.description: Decouples the rendering rate from the packet rate. With this off, one value drives both and r_maxfps has no independent effect.
cl_async.label: Asynchronous rendering

cl_blend.description: Coloured flashes on hits and powerups. Off is calmer.
cl_blend.label: Screen effects

cl_gun.description: Your own weapon in view. Off gives a clearer picture.
cl_gun.label: Show weapon model

q2pro.note: Q2PRO clamps this to 10–125. The classic cl_maxfps 125 is therefore the ceiling, and anything above it is silently reduced — raise r_maxfps if you want more rendered frames.

valueNote.0: On Q2PRO 0 means "as fast as allowed", which for the physics rate is MAX_PHYS_HZ, i.e. 125.

r1q2.note: With cl_async on, R1Q2 prints a warning above 100 and points you at r_maxfps instead; a high packet rate also risks a flood kick from the server.

valueNote.0: R1Q2 does not read 0 as "unlimited". The change callback clamps anything below 5 up to 5, leaving you at 5 packets per second — the server will drop or kick you for not sending enough updates.

vanilla.note: Vanilla has no asynchronous mode: this one value caps everything, and nothing clamps it.

cl_maxfps.description: Caps the local tick (packets and physics). In Quake 2 this rate affects jump height, which is why 125 is the classic compromise. On engines with asynchronous rendering it governs the packet rate only — the render rate is r_maxfps.
cl_maxfps.label: Max FPS (packets / physics)

cl_noskins.description: Gives every player the same model, which makes them easier to read.
cl_noskins.label: Uniform skins

cl_run.description: Without this you move at walking speed by default.
cl_run.label: Always run

q2pro.note: Only applies while connected and with the menu closed; scr_alpha scales the whole HUD separately.

con_alpha.description: How see-through the console is while connected to a server.
con_alpha.label: Console transparency

flag.clamped: {{engine}} clamps {{name}} to {{range}} and silently uses {{bound}} instead.
flag.otherAbsent: {{engine}}, also assigned, does not have {{name}} at all.
flag.otherNoRange: {{engine}}, also assigned, has no clamp range on record for {{name}}.
flag.otherPlainValue: {{engine}}, also assigned, documents nothing special about {{value}}.

fov.description: Viewing angle in degrees. 90 is the engine default; most players use 100–120 for a wider view. Very high values distort heavily.
fov.label: Field of view (FOV)

vanilla.note: Vanilla ships this off, which is why an unconfigured 3.20 engine feels broken to anyone used to a modern build.

freelook.description: Permanent look-around with the mouse. Should always be on.
freelook.label: Mouselook

q2pro.note: Q2PRO treats only the exact value 1 as "full dynamic lighting"; other non-zero values light entities but skip lightmap updates.

gl_dynamic.description: Light thrown by shots and explosions.
gl_dynamic.label: Dynamic lighting

q2pro.note: Q2PRO multiplies this by gl_modulate_world for world lightmaps and by gl_modulate_entities for models, so the effective brightness is a product of two cvars. On the gloom mod it also cheat-protects the extra ones.

r1q2.note: R1Q2 already ships this at 2 and archives it, so a competitive config usually does not need to set it at all.

gl_modulate.description: Scales level lighting up. The usual way to make dark corners visible.
gl_modulate.label: Brightness (lightmaps)

q2pro.note: Flagged CVAR_FILES on Q2PRO: textures are reloaded on change, so it needs a vid_restart to apply.

gl_picmip.description: Higher values make textures muddier but let enemies stand out more clearly.
gl_picmip.label: Texture detail

gl_polyblend.description: Extra colour wash underwater and when taking damage.
gl_polyblend.label: Colour overlay

gl_swapinterval.description: Prevents tearing but adds input latency.
gl_swapinterval.label: VSync

q2pro.note: Q2PRO adds MAG_NEAREST — trilinear minification with nearest magnification, i.e. crisp up close without aliasing at distance. Vanilla and R1Q2 reject the name and keep their previous filter.

gl_texturemode.description: Texture smoothing. NEAREST gives the hard retro look.
gl_texturemode.label: Texture filter

hand.description: Which side the weapon is drawn on.
hand.label: Weapon hand
hand.warning: The value 2 (centred / hidden) is implemented by the game DLL, not by the engine, so it depends on the mod being played rather than on the engine.

m_pitch.description: A negative value inverts the Y axis.
m_pitch.label: Vertical mouse direction

msg.description: How many server and kill messages are shown.
msg.label: Message filter

name.description: Your name in game. Shows up on the scoreboard and in chat.
name.label: Player name

valueNote.0: On Q2PRO 0 means unlimited: the frame-time helper falls back to MAX_REF_HZ, giving a 1000 FPS cap. This is also the Q2PRO default.

r1q2.note: R1Q2 already defaults to 1000, so leaving this alone is the uncapped case.

valueNote.0: R1Q2 does not read 0 as "unlimited". The change callback clamps anything below 5 up to 5, so the renderer is pinned at 5 FPS and the game stutters badly. The gate itself divides by the value, which is why the clamp has to exist at all.

r_maxfps.description: Caps the rendering rate separately from the packet rate. Only has an independent effect while cl_async is on.
r_maxfps.label: Render FPS cap

rate.description: Bytes per second the server may send. 25000 is a good value on any modern connection.
rate.label: Network rate

sensitivity.description: How far the view turns per unit of mouse movement.
sensitivity.label: Mouse sensitivity

q2pro.note: Without a hardware gamma ramp Q2PRO applies gamma to the textures themselves and flags the cvar CVAR_FILES, so a change only takes effect after vid_restart.

actions.aliasDuplicate: {{count}} entries resolve to the same alias name “{{name}}” ({{entries}}). Quake II only keeps the last definition it reads – whichever binding calls this name reaches only that one, never the others.
actions.aliasSelfReference: “{{entry}}” runs “{{command}}”, which is its own alias name “{{name}}”. The line is written exactly as you wrote it, but that command calls the entry back into itself – so either a built-in command of the same name wins and the entry never runs, or Quake II loops until it gives up. Remove that command, give the entry its own alias name, or leave it if you meant it.
actions.aliasShadowsCommand: “{{entry}}” resolves to the alias name “{{name}}”, which is already a built-in command or cvar. Quake II would define an alias that calls itself, so pressing the key runs nothing new. Give it its own alias name.
actions.aliasUnreferenced: The alias “{{name}}” is not called by anything in this profile. It is still written to the config file, but nothing ever runs it.
actions.pressWithoutRelease: “{{entry}}” is a press command (“{{name}}”) with no matching release alias. Quake II keeps running it until something else stops it, since there is nothing bound to run on key-up. Add a matching release alias, or recreate this as a press/release entry so the pair can never drift apart.
actions.releaseWithoutPress: “{{entry}}” is a release command (“{{name}}”) with no matching press alias. Nothing in this profile ever triggers it. Add a matching press alias, or recreate this as a press/release entry so the pair can never drift apart.
actions.toggleCrossWired: “{{dispatch}}”, “{{first}}” and “{{second}}” look like a toggle, but the two states are cross-wired: a working one has “{{first}}” hand control to “{{second}}” and “{{second}}” hand it back to “{{first}}”, and these do not – so the switch never loops between its two states. Recreate it as a toggle entry, or fix the “alias {{dispatch}} …” line at the end of each state so that each one points at the other.
actions.undefinedAlias: “{{action}}” calls “{{alias}}”, but no alias with that name exists in this profile any more. The bind still gets written, but pressing the key runs nothing.

cvar.absent: {{engine}} does not know {{name}}. The line is still written into the config file, but the engine skips it silently – nothing else happens.
cvar.absentFix: Remove the line, or leave it if this config is deliberately shared with another engine that does use {{name}}.
cvar.choiceRejected: {{engine}} does not accept {{name}} {{value}}. Only {{accepted}} understands this value – {{engine}} rejects the name and keeps whatever was set before.
cvar.noteErrorFix: Use an explicit value inside the normal range instead of {{value}}.
cvar.outOfRange: {{name}} {{value}} is outside what {{engine}} accepts. {{engine}} expects {{name}} between {{min}} and {{max}}.
cvar.outOfRangeClamped: {{name}} {{value}} is outside what {{engine}} accepts. {{engine}} clamps {{name}} to {{min}}-{{max}} and silently uses {{bound}} instead.

empty.noFacts: This profile is only assigned to {{engines}}, which the launcher has no source-cited limits or cvar facts for. Assign it to an R1Q2, Q2PRO or original Quake II installation to validate it.
empty.unassigned: This profile is not assigned to any installation, so there is no engine to check it against. Assign it to an installation and its findings appear here.

structure.aliasCycle: The aliases {{chain}} call each other in a loop. Quake II counts nested alias expansions and stops after {{max}} of them, so the loop eats the whole budget and everything queued behind it is dropped. Break the loop.
structure.aliasDepth: Running “{{name}}” expands {{depth}} aliases one inside the other. Quake II only expands {{max}} levels deep in a single pass and discards the rest, so the end of this chain never runs. Flatten it into fewer steps.
structure.aliasDuplicate: The alias “{{name}}” is defined a second time on line {{line}} of {{file}}. The later definition silently replaces the earlier one, so whatever used the first version now quietly does something else. Rename one of the two.
structure.aliasSpace: The alias name “{{name}}” contains a space (line {{line}} of {{file}}). The engine reads the name up to the first space and treats the rest as an argument, so this alias can never be called by the name it was given. Use underscores instead of spaces.
structure.aliasTooLong: The alias name “{{name}}” is {{length}} characters long. Quake II copies an alias name into a fixed buffer (MAX_ALIAS_NAME) and rejects anything longer with “Alias name is too long”, so this alias is never created at all. Use at most {{max}} characters.
structure.lineTooLong: Line {{line}} of {{file}} is {{bytes}} bytes long. Quake II reads a config line into a {{limit}}-byte buffer, so this line is thrown away (or cut in half) before it can run. Split it into several shorter lines.
structure.quoteBroken: The value on line {{line}} of {{file}} contains a quotation mark of its own ({{quotes}} in one value instead of the opening and closing pair). Quake II has no escape character inside a quoted value – the first quotation mark after the opening one ends it – so the remainder of the line is read as stray commands. Remove the quotation marks from the value.
structure.sizeOverCompressedDiscarded: {{file}} still measures {{bytes}} bytes after this engine strips comments and collapses whitespace ({{rawBytes}} bytes on disk), more than the {{limit}} bytes its command buffer holds. It rejects the file as a whole, so nothing in it takes effect.
structure.sizeOverCompressedTruncated: {{file}} still measures {{bytes}} bytes after this engine strips comments and collapses whitespace ({{rawBytes}} bytes on disk), more than the {{limit}} bytes its command buffer holds. It cuts the file off at that point, so the rest silently never runs.
structure.sizeOverDiscarded: {{file}} is {{bytes}} bytes, more than the {{limit}} bytes this engine's command buffer holds. It refuses a config that does not fit rather than applying part of it, so not one line of this file takes effect. Move settings you do not need out of the profile.
structure.sizeOverTruncated: {{file}} is {{bytes}} bytes, more than the {{limit}} bytes this engine's command buffer holds. It cuts the file off at the limit and only mentions it on the console, so everything past that point silently never runs.
structure.sizeWarn: {{file}} uses {{bytes}} of the {{limit}} bytes this engine's command buffer holds ({{percent}}%). There is little room left – a few more settings and the end of the file stops being read.
structure.sizeWarnCompressed: {{file}} uses {{bytes}} of the {{limit}} bytes this engine's command buffer holds ({{percent}}%), measured after comments are stripped and whitespace collapsed ({{rawBytes}} bytes on disk). There is little room left – a few more settings and the file stops fitting.
